rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only models with single-profile data. This configuration tests the simplest possible RNA encoder (PCA) without image data, isolating the impact of RNA representation and profile setting. It clarifies whether RNA-only models can achieve reasonable performance, providing critical evidence for later comparisons with multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with pca_n2000 achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of switching to multiprofile while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder unchanged, isolating the effect of profile setting. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether multiprofile improves performance, a key design choice with potential for significant impact.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation clarifies if encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It isolates the effect of representation (RNA encoder) in a promising direction (multiprofile), balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation achieve the highest accuracy (0.650). This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline improves performance, clarifying if multimodal approaches can outperform unimodal ones. It isolates the effect of adding image modality while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation consistent with prior successes.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieves 0.65 accuracy, while multimodal approaches like config_030 (0.63) underperform. This experiment tests whether using a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion (vs. concat in config_030) can improve performance. It isolates the impact of image encoder quality and fusion strategy, addressing key uncertainties about multimodal effectiveness without changing too many factors at once.

Existing evidence shows that using the imagenet_vit_l image encoder with weighted fusion (config_037) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (while keeping the same image encoder and weighted fusion) further improves performance. This isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, and could reveal if more complex aggregation improves results without changing other factors.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high performance (0.725 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more complex model) in the same multimodal setup could improve performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This addresses uncertainty about whether advanced RNA encoders outperform scvi_n200 in this context, while keeping other components consistent to focus on the key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 (config_005) outperforms pca_n2000 (config_002) in rna_only/multiprofile settings. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool (config_005) to transformer (config_006) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly addresses a key design choice with minimal changes, providing insight into whether transformer aggregation could further enhance performance for scvi_n200.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve 0.653 accuracy, while multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) reach 0.725. This experiment tests RNA-only with scgpt encoder and transformer aggregation, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200). It clarifies whether more complex RNA representations improve performance, balancing exploration of critical design choices while building on existing RNA-only insights.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_039). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 maintains performance, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. It leverages the current best RNA encoder and fusion strategy while exploring a simpler image encoder, addressing uncertainty about which image encoder is more effective for this task.
